“One of the problems that the marijuana reform movement consistently faces is that everyone wants to talk about what marijuana does, but no one ever wants to look at what marijuana prohibition does.” William F. Buckley Jr.

 

Recently, the Wall Street Journal’s Editorial Board has demonstrated an unhealthy obsession with Cannabis, printing a series of embarrassing unsigned rants that I have tried to address as politely as possible.

See To The Editors Of The Editorial Page Of The Wall Street Journal Regarding “Potheads Head For The Emergency Room”. Dehumanizing Others Dehumanizes Yourself

 

They were triggered — like most of the Prohibitionist posse — by the horrifying prospect that President Trump would issue an Executive Order that the DEA begin the process of reclassifying marijuana to acknowledge that marijuana has medical uses, thereby sending the wrong message to emotionally unstable teenagers, who would then use vast amounts of super strong weed and become addicted and schizophrenic. Or something like that.

 

By the happiest of coincidences, this coincided with the fiftieth anniversary of the first Cannabis “coffee shop” in The Netherlands, a mythical country where people puff on magic dragons. Or something like that.

Meanwhile Back In Amsterdam: The Fiftieth Anniversary Of The Bulldog, The First “CoffeeShop”

 

In 2001, Paul Gigot, a genuinely distinguished Conservative journalist became the head of the Journal’s Editorial Board. However, in 2002, the Journal published a Prohibitionist editorial that had the usual misinformation (lies) about cannabis in The Netherlands.

From July 18, 2002

See

My Thanks to the Editors of The Wall Street Journal For Lying to Their Readers (Again) -- Giving Me The Opportunity To Explain Dutch Cannabis Policies (Again). Reporting from Haarlem, The Netherlands.

 

“Meanwhile -- though getting much less U.S. media attention -- the Dutch are having second thoughts about their own famously liberal marijuana laws. Last week the Netherlands announced a plan to crack down on the legal " coffee " houses where you can buy cannabis along with your cappuccino.

Marijuananews note: That wasn’t true then, and it certainly isn’t true now.)

 

The arguments for decriminalizing marijuana are well known and not without appeal. And yet the evidence emerging in countries that have legalized (the Netherlands, Switzerland, Belgium) supports the view that decriminalization leads to rising drug use and higher crime rates.

 

Marijuananews note: Cannabis is still technically illegal in The Netherlands, but it has never been legal to sell it in Belgium or Switzerland. On the other hand, personal use quantities are decriminalized in Belgium, which has an open EU border with The Netherlands.

 

Marijuananews note:

As for decriminalizing marijuana leading to rising (hard) drug use…

“According to the European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction, drug-related deaths have increased in Europe since 2013, from 4,400 to almost 7,000 cases in 2022. Those deaths occurred mostly in the age group 25 to 44 years and among men. Ireland was the country registering the highest number of drug-induced deaths, followed by Estonia and Norway. None of these countries have legalized cannabis.

 

The Journal continues: Britain has its own bad example in the form of a pilot liberalization in Lambeth, which includes the drugs-ridden south London neighborhood of Brixton. Labour MP Kate Hoey, whose constituency includes Brixton, reports that drug dealers are pushing hard drugs openly on the streets.

Marijuananews note: What really happened? Well, a pilot policy was introduced by Metropolitan police commander Brian Paddick in 2001, and  limited to an area with a predominantly black population so that persons in possession of a personal use quantity of cannabis were “warned” instead of arrested and the cannabis was confiscated.

See

Crime Declined Sharply London Area With De Facto Decrim. The Narcs Caught In Yet Another Lie. Surprise! Surprise!

 

Police report an 11% increase in trafficking offenses -- though, to be fair, it wasn't clear whether that was because there are more dealers in the area or more cops. For the U.S., the lesson would appear to be to beware legalizers bearing British gifts.

Marijuananews note: “Legalizers”? The policy of not arresting someone with personal use quantities equals “legalization”?? Written by an “imprisoner”? A “strip searcher”?

 

Mr. Blair's proposal may sail through the House of Commons, but we're willing to wager that like the Dutch the British will regret the decision once they notice the rise in drug use.

The U.S. is better off just saying no.

 

Marijuananews note: It didn’t sail through Parliament, but that is a long story for another time. Cannabis is still not decriminalized, but…

From 2016, “Just one in four cannabis users are charged and arrests have fallen by almost 50% since 2010, new figures show”

“Huge disparity in how police forces across England and Wales tackle possession of class B drug revealed. And though the number of people facing charges after being caught with cannabis has fallen, there remains a stark contrast in how people of different races are treated.

A joint report by the London School of Economics and drug law reform charity Release revealed that in London black people were more than five times more likely to be charged with cannabis possession than white people.

 

Meanwhile, Scotland’s drug deaths remain worst in Europe amid ‘concerning’ 12% increase. Government pledges to step up efforts to tackle the problem as figures show the number of deaths rose to 1,172 in 2023.

And The Skunk At UK’s Reefer Madness Party: Mental Illness Second Worst While Cannabis Use Goes Down

 

And , meanwhile back in The Netherlands… 23 years later, the coffee shops are still open and The Netherlands ranks fifth or lower in cannabis consumption in various surveys of national cannabis consumption.

And

Dutch youth continues to rank among the healthiest and happiest in Europe - News

May 19,  2020 — Dutch youths also reported considerably less psychosomatic disorders (such as headaches and unhappiness) than their European age-group peers.

And

European Study Shows Potency of Prohibitionist Propaganda. CBS and The AP Lie to the American People About the Dutch. Surprise!
